entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wahibre Ibiau was an ancient Egyptian petty king, perhaps of the 13th Dynasty, during the Second Intermediate Period. He may have reigned for about 10 years according to the Turin King List.


His significance lies in the tumultuous politics of ancient Egypt, where various dynasties clashed over power. Wahibre Ibiau's rule marked a brief respite for the 13th Dynasty, but his reign was short-lived and ultimately unsuccessful in preventing the rise of the Hyksos.


The core events of his rule were marked by military campaigns against the Hyksos, but these efforts were ultimately in vain. Despite this, Wahibre Ibiau's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the 13th Dynasty on ancient Egyptian society and politics.







The Second Intermediate Period was a transformative era in ancient Egyptian history, marked by the rise and fall of various dynasties and the eventual reunification of Egypt under the 18th Dynasty. Wahibre Ibiau's reign was just one chapter in this broader narrative, highlighting the complexities and challenges of ancient Egyptian politics.
